svg.title: How the Bible's ontology is made, stored and used
svg.desc: A four-band architecture picture: how canonical ids, stories, situations and readings are built; the graph and skills registry that store them; the live Ask harness that reads them; and the harness ideas ASTER, SPARQL-LLM, GTA-RAG and decide-and-refuse, each with how far it has got.
svg.text: From Hebrew and Greek to an answer: how the Bible's ontology is made and used
Canonical ids hold it together. A model proposes, code checks, and every record says how sure it is. The harness reads it through skills.
built from committed sources, by code and small models
Layers join on ids, never on names.
nothing here is written at ask time
the ontology gathers and checks; a model writes; code proves the verses
how each new idea uses the ontology, and how far it has got
On 28 story questions, scored by code: 25% without graph research, 86 to 93% with it. On 100 real questions, mostly "Who was...": 2 better, 3 worse, 95 the same.
